periods_leaf0.question: Assessment: Menstrual irregularity
periods_leaf0.explanation: Among 645 similar MedDialog consultations with these answers, doctors most often discussed: Menstrual irregularity (85%), Hormonal imbalance or PCOS (10%). This counts what doctors mentioned in their replies; it is not a diagnosis.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:
Cycles that come early, late, or not at all are common with stress, weight change, thyroid or hormone problems, and after stopping contraception.

In similar MedDialog consultations, doctors most often discussed: Menstrual irregularity (85%), Hormonal imbalance or PCOS (10%).
homeCareInstructions: Keep a calendar of start dates and flow
Take a pregnancy test if sex has occurred and a period is late
Aim for regular sleep, meals, and exercise
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: See a doctor if you miss 3 periods in a row, bleed very heavily, or have severe pain.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:
Irregular periods with acne, extra facial hair, or weight gain can point to PCOS or another hormonal cause. Blood tests and an ultrasound help confirm it.

In similar MedDialog consultations, doctors most often discussed: Hormonal imbalance or PCOS (61%), Pregnancy (43%), Thyroid disorder (12%).
homeCareInstructions: Ask your doctor about hormone and thyroid blood tests and a pelvic ultrasound
Regular exercise and a balanced diet help even if weight changes are small
Keep a calendar of your periods
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Book a visit if periods stop for 3 months, bleeding is very heavy, or you are trying to conceive.

In similar MedDialog consultations, doctors most often discussed: Allergic reaction or hives (26%), Allergic rhinitis or allergy (25%), Eczema or dermatitis (10%).
homeCareInstructions: Avoid the suspected trigger such as a new food, medicine, soap, or insect bite

backpain_leaf0.question: Assessment: Injury or fracture
backpain_leaf0.explanation: Among 1251 similar MedDialog consultations with these answers, doctors most often discussed: Injury or fracture (30%), Lumbar strain or muscle spasm (13%), Slipped disc or disc bulge (12%). This counts what doctors mentioned in their replies; it is not a diagnosis.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:
Pain, bruising, or swelling after a fall, twist, or heavy lift can be a sprain, strain, or sometimes a fracture. A doctor can decide whether an X-ray is needed.

In similar MedDialog consultations, doctors most often discussed: Injury or fracture (30%), Lumbar strain or muscle spasm (13%), Slipped disc or disc bulge (12%).
homeCareInstructions: Rest the area and avoid heavy lifting or weight-bearing if it hurts
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth for 15 minutes several times a day for the first 2 days
Compression and raising the limb can reduce swelling
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Go to urgent care today if you cannot bear weight, the shape looks wrong, or there is numbness or severe pain.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:

In similar MedDialog consultations, doctors most often discussed: Neuropathy or nerve compression (34%), Slipped disc or disc bulge (18%), Vitamin deficiency (10%).
homeCareInstructions: Avoid staying in the same position for long periods
Ask about blood tests for sugar, vitamin B12, and thyroid
Protect numb areas from heat and injury
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Seek urgent care for sudden weakness, trouble walking, loss of bladder or bowel control, or numbness on one side of the body.
